newsitem.title: USA: U.S. talks tough on Albania election.
newsitem.headline: U.S. talks tough on Albania election.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it would not tolerate attempts by Albania's opposing political factions to impede parliamentary elections set for June 29.
Secretary of State Madeleine Albright held talks at the State Department with Albania's interim Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and spokesman Nicholas Burns said that would be her message.

"The secretary will assure the (Albanian) delegation that the United States and Europe will not tolerate attempts by one party or faction to delay or obstruct the important process of the preparations for the elections," he said.

Albright invited Fino to the United States "to express her strong support for the forces of moderation and consensus in Albania as the country prepares for what we hope will be free and fair parliamentary elections on June 29," Burns said.
Under an agreement brokered by European envoy Franz Vranitzky, Albania's 10 main political parties agreed to break an impasse by holding early elections in June.
Fino heads a nine-party government of national reconciliation set up in March to halt Albania's drift to anarchy and prepare for elections.

In their meeting, Albright planned to "highlight the substantial investment which the international community is currently making in Albania to help it resolve its political problems, its economic problems, and...emphasise the importance of these elections as a means to re-establish public confidence in Albanian governmental institutions," Burns said.
